rationale: The registry packetSet lists supporting_timeline as a required component with outputStrategy 'custom_pleading' and no officialFormId.
The controlling review records that what LegalEase can prepare at this stage is 'the application and the supporting timeline'.

The timeline exists because the one-year period runs from the expiration of the probation term and not from the dismissal — the registry carries that as an express packet instruction, and the two dates are usually different.
It is drafted as a container of participant-confirmed dates only. It computes nothing and concludes nothing.

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: The clock: not less than one year, beginning to run immediately upon the expiration of the term of probation. It runs from the expiration of probation, not from the dismissal.

The predicate the submission rests on: the court, without entering a judgment of guilt, deferred further proceedings and placed the participant on probation conditioned on successful completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program under § 17C-5A-3a.

After a period of not less than one year beginning to run immediately on the expiration of the term of probation, the person may apply to the court for an order expunging all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction, except those maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles; a person previously convicted of a felony may not make that motion; objections are filed within 30 days of service, and if objections are filed the court holds a hearing and, if it determines there was no serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation, it shall order the expungement.

qaProhibitedTermsNote: Four groups, each for a distinct sourced reason. (1) 'petition' and 'petitioner': every West Virginia Judiciary expungement form catalogued in the committed state pack and named in the compiled profile is a petition or motion under § 61-11-25 or § 61-11-26 — a different statute with a different fee regime, a different service list, a once-per-lifetime limit under § 61-11-26(o), and an express § 61-11-26b bar on expunging DUI convictions. Section 17C-5-2b says the defendant may MOVE the court and the person may APPLY to the court, and the registry names the instruments a motion and an application. A document styling itself a petition would read as the § 61-11-26 packet the participant must not be sold. (2) 'seal', 'sealed', 'sealing': sealing of court records is the § 61-11-26 remedy — the profile records that on a granted § 61-11-26 order the court orders court records sealed and agency records expunged. Section 17C-5-2b(g) speaks only of expunging official records and says nothing about sealing. (3) 'destroy', 'destroyed', 'destruction', 'erase': the committed state pack's own never-say list forbids telling a participant that this destroys every record or that no one can ever see it again, and the profile records that legally authorised criminal-history checks and law-enforcement-type job applications can still reach expunged convictions. (4) 'pardon', 'vacate', 'vacatur', 'acquittal', 'acquitted', 'pretrial diversion', 'deferred adjudication': each names a different West Virginia route — § 5-1-16a pardon relief, § 61-14-9 trafficking vacatur, the § 61-11-25 acquittal/dismissal motion on SCA-C903, § 61-11-22 pretrial diversion (from which DUI is expressly excluded) and § 61-11-22a deferred adjudication. A § 17C-5-2b deferral is none of them, and using their vocabulary would misdescribe the relief and blur the routing boundary. Scope: these terms are prohibited in the RENDERED DOCUMENT TEXT of this component only. Several of them necessarily appear in participant-facing routing and disclosure copy, where they do necessary work — telling the participant that this is not the conviction-expungement route and that an expunged record is still reachable by legally authorised checks.

counselFlags.statement: The one-year window in § 17C-5-2b(g)(1) runs from the expiration of the term of probation, not from the dismissal. The two dates are usually different and the dismissal is the more visible one, so the wrong date is the obvious failure mode. The registry requires written confirmation of the probation-expiry date from the supervising probation office or the clerk, and requires the participant's own answer to be checked against it. This route computes nothing: it states the participant's two dates side by side and never asserts that the year has run.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That any waiting-period computation downstream measures from probation expiry, never from the dismissal date.

counselFlags.statement: What LegalEase cannot complete: the Division of Motor Vehicles certification that the test and lock program was successfully completed. Section 17C-5-2b(c) requires the motion to dismiss to be supported by it, so the motion cannot go in without it, but it is an agency document the participant obtains by asking the Division of Motor Vehicles. No form number, no request letter and no template is recorded for it anywhere in the sources, so none is drafted and no agency_request_letter unit exists in this route. LegalEase does not obtain, receive or inspect it, and no drafted document characterises what it says.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no pipeline stage produces or files the motion to dismiss without the participant holding the Division of Motor Vehicles certification.

counselFlags.statement: No West Virginia Judiciary form exists for either the § 17C-5-2b(c) motion to dismiss or the § 17C-5-2b(g) application to expunge. The Court Forms index was read at source on 2026-08-06 and publishes exactly five expungement forms — SCA-C900, SCA-C903, SCA-C906, SCA-C907 and SCA-C912 — none of which is a § 17C-5-2b filing; the committed state pack catalogues the same five and ties each to § 61-11-25 or § 61-11-26. On that basis the controlling review's build blocker is answered in the negative and every court document in this route is a custom pleading. Whether an unpublished local form is used in some courts was not tested.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether any court uses an unpublished local form for a § 17C-5-2b filing.

counselFlags.statement: The two stages must never be merged into one filing. The registry models them as separate units because the required contents, the timing and the legal effect all differ: the subsection (c) motion needs the defendant's affidavit and the Division of Motor Vehicles certification and produces dismissal and discharge without adjudication of guilt; the subsection (g) application cannot be made until a further year has run from the expiration of probation, is barred outright by any prior felony conviction, and produces expungement of the criminal record. Unit 1 must have produced a dismissal before unit 2 becomes available at all. The words expunge, expunged and expungement are prohibited in the unit-1 document text for exactly this reason.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the pipeline cannot emit the subsection (g) application at the same time as the subsection (c) motion, and that stageNeeded gates which components are produced.

TIMELINE IN SUPPORT OF APPLICATION FOR AN ORDER EXPUNGING RECORDS PURSUANT TO W. VA. CODE § 17C-5-2b(g)(1).

Dated entries only, each one a participant answer the registry requires to be checked against a document the participant obtains: the date the court deferred the proceedings and imposed probation (checked against the deferral order); the probation term as that order states it; the date the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program was successfully completed (checked against the Division of Motor Vehicles certification); the date the charges were dismissed and the participant discharged (checked against the order of dismissal and discharge); and the date the probation term expired (checked against written confirmation from the probation office or the clerk). No date is computed, no interval is asserted, and the timeline never concludes that the one-year period has run — that is the court's determination.
Two citations: § 17C-5-2b(g)(1) for the one-year period and the date it runs from, and (a)/(b) for the deferral and probation the period is measured from.

provenance.profileSilenceNote: The compiled WV profile contains no occurrence of '17C-5-2b', 'Test and Lock', '17C-5A-3a' or any DUI-deferral pathway. Its only occurrences of '17C-5-2' are the single repeated statement that DUI under 17C-5-2 is excluded from pretrial diversion under 61-11-22. The seven pathways it enumerates are the 61-11-25 no-conviction route, 61-11-26 conviction expungement, the 61-11-26a accelerated route, the 60A-4-407 conditional discharge, 5-1-16a pardon relief, 61-14-9 trafficking vacatur and juvenile relief. This route therefore rests on the pinned registry entry; the profile and the committed state pack are used only for the West Virginia court-level, form-catalogue, intake-field and terminology facts they do record.
